newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly down, pork bellies off sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly down, pork bellies off sharply.

text.p: CME hogs closed mostly lower on selling linked to weakness in cash markets while pork bellies finished sharply down.
"All the news is weak," one dealer said, noting both product and cash hog prices were declining. "Everybody (all hog buyers) has what they need."
Cash hogs were expected to be $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower on Thursday after dropping $0.50 to $1.00 on Wednesday.
Floor sources said E.D. and F. Man International was a featured seller of both August and October hogs. Lind Waldock was also a noted seller of the two nearby months.
Iowa Grain was a late seller of December hogs.
Locals and Rand Financial Services' commercial desk were among August buyers, floor sources said.
August hogs closed 0.400 cent a lb lower at 79.950 cents with other months up 0.100 to down 0.200 cent.

Pork bellies closed lower with the July contract, which expires next week, falling the three-cent limit amid late long liquidation by Smith Barney. Floor sources said the pool of unfilled sell-orders in July totalled five cars.
Most active August ended 2.175 cents a lb lower at 81.100 cents with other months down 3.00 to 0.275 cents.
Cash-connected selling weakened August with USDA reporting at midday 14-16 lb supplies of cash bellies traded $3 lower at $85 per cwt.
There was talk that prices look set to dip further short-term with trade expected Thursday between $82 and $83.

Dealers noted CME's weekly out-of-town pork belly storage report, issued after the close Tuesday, showed a net out-movement of 2.914 million lbs, towards the upper end of the 2.5 to 3.0 million lb range of analysts' estimates.
